clusters.title: Large Multi-Functional Regulatory Supercluster: Transcription, RNA Processing, Ubiquitin-Proteasome, Signaling, and Cytoskeletal Organization
clusters.overall_function: This very large cluster encompasses a broad array of cellular regulatory functions including transcriptional regulation (Mediator complex, TAF/TFIID, SAGA, PRC1/2, NuRD, NELF), RNA processing and splicing (hnRNPs, SRSF, snRNPs, CELF, MBNL, RBM families), ubiquitin-proteasome system (FBXO/FBXL/FBXW F-box proteins, USPs, RNFs, UBE2/3/4 enzymes, CUL1/4/5), signal transduction (MAP3K/MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR via RPTOR/RICTOR, STAT family, Rho GEFs/GAPs, Wnt/beta-catenin via CTNNB1/AXIN), cytoskeletal and actin dynamics (MYO family, DIAPH, WASF, ARPC, FMNL), autophagy (ATG genes, WIPI1, RUBCN), vesicle trafficking (VPS, TRAPPC, SNX, AP complexes), DNA damage response (CHEK2, NBN, MDC1, XRCC1, RAD21, PARP family), and chromatin remodeling (KDM, SETDB, SMYD, ARID, PHF families). The cluster likely represents a co-regulated gene network active in proliferating or differentiating cells rather than a single coherent pathway.

clusters.rationale: The 2231-gene cluster centered on MYO9A contains an extraordinarily diverse set of gene families. Core regulatory machinery (Mediator, TFIID/TAF, SAGA, PRC1/2, NuRD, NELF, spliceosome, hnRNPs, ubiquitin E3 ligases, deubiquitinases) is broadly expressed and could co-cluster due to shared housekeeping expression patterns. However, the simultaneous presence of highly tissue-restricted programs—cardiac/skeletal muscle contractile proteins (TNNI, TNNT, TMOD, LMOD, RYR, CACNB), erythroid hemoglobins (HBA1/2, HBM, HBQ1, HBZ), germline piRNA/meiosis genes (PIWIL1/2/4, DAZL, HORMAD1/2, BOLL, TEX11), and neuronal synaptic genes (DLG1-4, MAGI2, UNC13A/B, NOVA1/2, STMN1-4)—is a strong indicator that this cluster is not biologically coherent. It likely represents an artifact of low clustering resolution, batch effects, or ambient RNA contamination mixing multiple cell type transcriptomes. The oncogenic and signaling components (CTNNB1, STAT3, MYCN, BRAF, PIK3CB, RPTOR/RICTOR) are real and functionally related but are diluted by the tissue-specific noise. Confidence is moderate-low due to the implausible co-clustering of mutually exclusive tissue programs.
recommended_followups: Re-cluster at higher resolution to split this supercluster into biologically coherent sub-modules (e.g., splicing, ubiquitin, mTOR, muscle, neuronal, germline)
Check for ambient RNA contamination (SoupX or similar) given hemoglobin gene presence
Perform pathway enrichment (GO, KEGG, Reactome) on sub-sampled gene sets to identify dominant functional themes

clusters.title: Large Cytoskeletal Scaffold, Signaling Hub, and Cell Division Regulatory Network
clusters.overall_function: This very large cluster encompasses a broad but interconnected set of biological functions centered on cytoskeletal organization, cell polarity, scaffold/adaptor signaling, centrosome/cilia biology, cell division and mitosis, DNA damage response, apoptosis regulation, immune signaling, and vesicle trafficking. Key themes include: (1) extensive cytoskeletal scaffolding via AKAP, CCDC, ANKRD, and PDZ-domain proteins; (2) centrosome/centriole/cilium assembly (CEP family, CFAP family, CCDC39/40, DNAAF proteins); (3) mitotic regulation (BUB1, CENP family, TACC, HAUS, PLK4, STIL, ASPM, KNL1, SGO1/2, INCENP, NUSAP1); (4) Rho/Rac GEF-GAP signaling (ARHGEF/ARHGAP families); (5) DNA damage and repair (BRCA1/2, FANCA/F/M, ATM pathway components, RMI1, SLX4); (6) apoptosis/BCL2 family; (7) immune/NF-kB signaling (IRAK1/2, IRF3/4/7/8/9, CARD family, STING1, NFKB inhibitors); (8) meiosis (SYCP1-3, SYCE, TEX genes, STRA8, MEI1/4); (9) vesicle/membrane trafficking (RAB11FIP, DENND, TBC1D, SNX families).

clusters.title: Calcium-Binding Proteins, Myosin Light Chains, S100 Family, and Mitochondrial Carriers (SLC25A)
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by three major functional groups: (1) EF-hand calcium-binding proteins spanning multiple subfamilies (calmodulins, S100 proteins, calbindins, parvalbumins, neuronal calcium sensors, CABP family, KCNIP/KChIPs, recoverin/GUCA family, calcineurin regulatory subunits); (2) myosin light chain proteins (MYL family) involved in muscle contraction and cytoskeletal regulation; and (3) the nearly complete SLC25A mitochondrial carrier family responsible for metabolite transport across the inner mitochondrial membrane. Additional members include histone H1 linker histones (H1-0 through H1-6) and HMGN chromatin-associated proteins. The co-clustering of these groups likely reflects shared EF-hand domain architecture and/or co-expression patterns rather than a single unified biological pathway.

Overall confidence is moderate due to the mixed nature of the cluster.

clusters.title: Broad Metabolic, Chromatin Remodeling, DNA Repair, and Cytoskeletal Regulation Supercluster

clusters.rationale: The cluster's representative gene ETFDH (electron transfer flavoprotein dehydrogenase) and the dominant gene sets — NDUFA/B/C/S subunits, UQCR subunits, COX subunits, ATP5 subunits, MRPL/MRPS ribosomal proteins, TIMM/TOMM import components, COQ biosynthesis genes, TCA cycle enzymes (PDHA1, DLST, SUCLG1, SDHC/D), and fatty acid oxidation enzymes (ACADVL, ACSL1, CPT2, ECHS1, ECI1) — strongly indicate a mitochondrial metabolism and OXPHOS core. The cluster is partially coherent around a 'metabolic enzyme' theme but is too large and contains functionally distant genes (neuronal receptors, WNT/SHH signaling, acute phase proteins) to be considered a tight functional module. This likely reflects a co-expression-based clustering that captures broadly expressed metabolic and mitochondrial genes across multiple tissue types.

clusters.title: Transcription Factor & Chromatin Regulatory Supercluster
clusters.overall_function: This cluster is dominated by transcription factors (TFs) spanning virtually all major TF families—HOX, FOX, SOX, PAX, KLF/SP, GATA, NR (nuclear receptors), ETS, bHLH, bZIP, ZNF/ZBTB, T-box, POU, RUNX, NKX, DLX, IRX, CREB, MEF2, TEAD, SMAD-related, and many others—alongside chromatin remodelers (ARID1A/B, CHD7/8, CREBBP, EP300, KMT2A/C/D, SETD1A/B, SIN3A, HDAC4/5/7/9, SRCAP, EP400), coactivators/corepressors (NCOR1, NCOA5/6, TLE1-5, MAML1-3, BCOR), RNA-binding proteins with regulatory roles (CPEB1-4, RBFOX1-3, RBM family, YTHDF1/3), and nuclear pore components (NUP98, NUP214, NUP153). The cluster represents the broad transcriptional regulatory machinery governing cell identity, differentiation, and gene expression programs.

cancer_cell_type_prediction_relevance: Leukemia/lymphoma: MYC, BCL6, RUNX1T1, ETV6, FLI1, ERG, NUP98 fusions, KMT2A rearrangements are hallmark oncogenes in hematologic malignancies

Pancreatic cancer: PDX1, GATA6, KLF5, MYC, KRAS-downstream TFs relevant to PDAC

Mixed lineage TFs: cluster contains TFs from virtually every developmental lineage (neural, hematopoietic, endodermal, mesodermal) suggesting co-expression-independent grouping possibly based on GO annotation or protein domain similarity

Non-TF contaminants: NUP proteins (NUP98, NUP214, NUP153, NUP54, NUP58, NUP62), SEC proteins (SEC16A/B, SEC24C/D), RBM/CPEB RNA-binding proteins, BAG3/4 (chaperones), LATS1 (kinase), MAP2K4 (kinase), WNK1/2 (kinases), LGALS3 (lectin), COL17A1 (collagen) are functionally distinct from TFs
Housekeeping TFs mixed with tissue-specific: SP1, YY1AP1, TBP, GTF2A1, GTF3A are general transcription factors mixed with highly tissue-restricted TFs

Paralogs inflating cluster: Many gene families (39 HOX genes, 40+ FOX genes, 30+ ZNF/ZBTB genes) may be co-clustered due to sequence/domain similarity rather than functional co-expression
clusters.rationale: Cluster 7 contains 1101 genes that are overwhelmingly transcription factors and chromatin regulators spanning all major TF families. The representative gene BAZ2A is a chromatin reader/remodeler consistent with this theme. The cluster includes complete or near-complete representation of HOX, FOX, SOX, PAX, KLF, GATA, NR, ETS, bHLH, bZIP, ZNF, T-box, POU, NKX, DLX, IRX, CREB, MEF2, and TEAD families. This breadth strongly suggests the cluster was formed based on shared functional annotation (transcription factor/DNA-binding activity) or protein domain similarity rather than tight co-expression in a specific cell type. While internally coherent at the level of 'transcriptional regulation,' the cluster is too heterogeneous to represent a single biological program or cell state. Non-TF members (NUPs, kinases, RNA-binding proteins, a collagen) represent likely contamination or guilt-by-association clustering. The cluster has high utility for identifying transcriptional regulatory programs broadly but limited specificity for any single cell type or disease context without sub-clustering.

Investigate NUP98, EWSR1, and KMT2A as fusion oncogene hubs within this cluster for cancer perturbation modeling
Apply SCENIC or similar TF activity inference to determine which TFs in this cluster are active regulators vs. merely expressed

clusters.title: Broad Cellular Housekeeping and Stress-Response Supercluster
clusters.overall_function: This large cluster encompasses a highly diverse set of genes spanning ubiquitin-proteasome system components, DNA damage response and repair, RNA processing, vesicular trafficking, mitochondrial function, lipid metabolism, protein quality control (ER stress/UPR), cell signaling (mTOR, TBK1, STK11/LKB1), autophagy, nucleocytoplasmic transport, and ciliogenesis. No single dominant pathway is evident; instead the cluster appears to aggregate broadly expressed housekeeping and stress-response genes.
cell_type_relevance: Non-specific: genes are broadly expressed across many cell types
Cycling/proliferating cells: DNA repair (ATM, FANCD2, MLH1, PRKDC), replication (POLA2, PRIM1, MCM9), and cell cycle (CCNE2, PRC1, STAG1) genes suggest relevance to proliferating states

cell_tissue_of_origin_prediction_relevan: Low specificity: the breadth of functions makes tissue-of-origin inference unreliable from this cluster alone

mTOR pathway (MTOR, TSC2, RHEB, PTEN, STK11/STRADA) relevant to mTOR-driven cancers (renal, lung adenocarcinoma, endometrial)

clusters.rationale: The cluster representative TBK1 is an innate immune kinase, but the 1089-member gene list spans an implausibly broad range of biological functions including ciliogenesis (BBS genes, CFAP genes), DNA repair (ATM, FANC genes, MLH1), mTOR signaling (MTOR, TSC2, PTEN, STK11), RNA processing (CNOT1, SF3A1, INTS genes), lipid metabolism (HADHA, MTTP, LCAT), ER quality control (PDIA2-6, TMX1-4, EDEM1), autophagy (BECN1, ATG10/13), and many transmembrane proteins of unknown function (TMEM genes).
